audience.role: DSH users deciding whether the published Bundle supports their host

checks.note: The READMEs state the current support contract, changelogs preserve the version delta, and release notes explain the upgrade effect.
Readers can identify the exact supported DSH version, understand why the market card changes, and see that no runtime migration is required.
Market metadata is introduced through its visible card and installation effect before package-field details are named.
The documents separate reused runtime evidence from new package, publication, installation, and market-readback evidence.
The short patch release leads with the visible compatibility correction and keeps detailed prior runtime behavior in linked history.
English and Chinese independently state the same exact DSH range, metadata effect, evidence reuse, and pending public refresh.

limitations: Cold reader review is not package, registry, GitHub Release, installation, or market readback proof.
Runtime evidence is reused only because packaged JavaScript and Python behavior is unchanged; the new artifact still requires package and install checks.
The market card can be verified only after npm publication and catalog refresh.
